title: Repeated grip change does not establish added HbA1c prediction across two NHANES samples
abstract: We tested whether repeated-grip information discarded by the conventional maximum-strength summary improves prediction of concurrent glycated hemoglobin. A fixed model trained in 4,402 NHANES 2011–2012 adults was evaluated without target refitting in 4,893 adults from the separately sampled 2013–2014 release. Adding bilateral mean first-to-third trial change and its square changed examination-weighted HbA1c MSE from 0.7421175 to 0.7424483 percent-squared. Improvement, defined as baseline minus augmented MSE, was -0.0003309; paired target stratified-PSU bootstrap 95% interval [-0.0014991, 0.0006520]. Source-and-target coefficient-refit uncertainty also included zero. This is a negative result for a fixed representation and learning procedure, not evidence of equivalence or absence of all grip-related metabolic information. Same-program independent-sample testing is not independent-study or cross-platform validation.
